unsupported.what: the ordinal-logit simple slopes of system justification on petition category: original control b = -0.35, SE = 0.10, 95% CI [-0.54, -0.16], Wald = 13.08, p < .001 (Table 2); true control b = -0.26, p = .002 (p. 10)
unsupported.why: review 3 R3-M2: the authors fit MASS::polr(PetitionsORDINAL ~ SYSJ_mean * CONDITION) and read the simple slope at a reference level; the engine only has Pearson r, whose sign can be opposite to the ordinal-logit coefficient (a reproduced admissible case: r = -0.067 vs polr slope = +0.22). Sign equivalence is not demonstrated, so these are retained as printed results only, not scored (engine request moderated_regression, ordinal-logit variant)

cite.label: reported
cite.note: Table 2 (printed rotated; read from the page image and cross-checked against its reversed text layer): petitions, 'Control condition': b = -0.35, SE = 0.10, 95% asymptotic CI [-0.54, -0.16], Wald = 13.08, p < .001

cite.label: reported
cite.note: 'significant negative relationships between system justification and petition signing in the original (b = -0.35, p < .001) and true control conditions (b = -0.26, p = .002)'

unsupported.what: the pre-registered tests: system justification x condition on PEB intentions, original control vs system-preservation (b = 0.05, SE = 0.12, beta = .06, t(374) = 0.43, p = .670); the follow-up simple slopes were not run (non-significant interaction); original study b = 0.95, SE = 0.41, t(37) = 2.29, p = .03
unsupported.why: no engine op fits a linear model with a continuous moderator x condition interaction (engine request moderated_regression); only the OLS within-arm slope sign is scored (effect peb_slope_true)

unsupported.what: system justification x condition on the ordinal petition outcome (b = 0.37, SE = 0.13, 95% CI [0.12, 0.63], OR = 1.45, Wald = 8.20, p = .004; original b = 1.26, Wald = 5.01, p = .03), the system-preservation slope (b = 0.02, SE = 0.09, p = .783, n.s.), the negative binomial robustness checks (interaction b = 0.16, SE = 0.08, p = .035; original-control slope b = -0.53, SE = 0.18, p = .003; system-preservation slope b = -0.01, SE = 0.17, p = .930)
unsupported.why: moderated regression / ordinal logit / negative binomial models are not engine ops (engine request moderated_regression)

unsupported.what: the three-condition models (PEB: original vs true control b = 0.29, p = .015; system-preservation vs true control b = 0.34, p = .003; slopes true control b = -0.24 SE = .08 p = .003, original b = 0.05 SE = .09 p = .553, system-preservation b = 0.11 SE = .09 p = .213; petitions: original vs true control b = -0.09 p = .498, system-preservation vs true control b = 0.28 SE = .12 p = .021; slopes original -0.35 p < .001, true control -0.26 p = .002, system-preservation 0.02 p = .786)
unsupported.why: interaction terms and the n.s. slopes need a moderated-regression op (engine request moderated_regression); the true-control PEB slope (OLS) is scored on its sign; the ordinal-logit petition slopes are not scored (see the next entry)

unsupported.what: Table 5: model-predicted percentages of none / a few / most petitions at M +- 1 SD and M +- 1.5 SD of system justification, per condition; the M +- 1 SD comparisons of PEB intentions (system-preservation 4.30 vs true control 4.97 at M - 1SD, t(561) = -2.49, p = .025; 4.64 vs 4.21 at M + 1SD, t(561) = 1.65, p = .179); Johnson-Neyman regions (2.87 / 5.83; 7.48)
unsupported.why: predicted values of a fitted model at sample-dependent system-justification cut-offs: no engine op

unsupported.what: system justification by condition, F(2, 564) = 0.65, p = .521, eta2 = .002 (manipulation check); scale reliabilities (alpha = .93 PEB, .88 system justification); political orientation did not interact with condition (supplement); Cohen's-type and Wald statistics
unsupported.why: an omnibus F and reliability are not engine ops; the system-justification mean (M = 3.77, SD = 1.60, p. 12) is target sj_mean

unsupported.what: the supplementary analyses with exclusions (N = 447: 59 completed in under half the median time, 36 + 38 failed a naivety check, 67 non-naive, none failed the attention check)
unsupported.why: time on survey is not a recorded unit field of the replay and the attention / naivety answers are served but not used as exclusions; the paper's main analyses use the full sample (N = 567)
